Dustin Coffell

Libertarian candidate for State Auditor, Missouri · Challenger

Accountant; Chair of the Libertarian Party of Missouri

Dustin Coffell, of Lake Saint Louis, is the Libertarian nominee for Missouri State Auditor. He was unopposed in the Libertarian primary on August 4, 2026. He chairs the Libertarian Party of Missouri and faces incumbent Republican Scott Fitzpatrick and Democrat Quentin Wilson in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Coffell stands

Role of the auditor's office
Says the auditor is supposed to be the watchdog for taxpayers and that every dollar taken from paychecks should be accounted for. Says that work should not be partisan.
Independent oversight
Says his top priority is removing "even a whiff of politics" from the auditor's office. Argues that a voter would otherwise have politicians checking their own party's work.
Auditing state government
Says that if elected, he would like to see an audit of every state government department.
Working with the legislature
Says he wants to work with the General Assembly, the governor's office and executive agencies to cut what he calls superfluous spending.
State budget and taxes
On his campaign Facebook page, he says he wants Missouri residents to pay the lowest taxes possible.

Background

  • Chair, Libertarian Party of Missouri (current)
  • Libertarian candidate for Missouri House District 70, 2022 and 2024
  • Senior accountant at an agriculture company; about 8 years in corporate accounting
  • Worked in the casino industry for nearly a decade
  • B.S. in Accounting (2019) and M.S. in Accounting (2022); CPA candidate
